description: Adds a physics-style repulsion relaxation (overlap and wall forces, radii growing into free space), an exact LP radius step, and a short basin-hopping refinement, placed as a new construct_packing definition just before the EVOLVE-BLOCK-END marker so it overrides the old one without a multi-line SEARCH.

Adds a linearly decaying (0.1 to 0) quadratic pull toward a fixed 6-row staggered template layout during the multistart inflation relaxation only, with the basin-hopping stage and final LP step unregularised.

Adds a trust-region radius to the inflation relaxation's center steps, adapted by comparing predicted and actual decrease of the overlap-plus-wall penalty energy (grow 1.5x above 0.75, shrink 0.5x below 0.25, reject non-decreasing steps, stop below 1e-7).

Replaces the constructor with a two-phase search: a time-boxed coarse phase of many short inflation relaxations keeping the top five LP-scored packings, then a per-candidate stiff-penalty relaxation followed by a joint SLSQP solve over centers and radii, with the exact LP step and validity clipping applied to the best result.
Adds a fixed-seed random-subset block relaxation (8 circles moving at a time, others frozen, three cycles) to each phase-2 candidate before SLSQP and LP, to escape jammed local configurations.

Adds a hexagonal-lattice start (30 staggered points, the 4 most corner-ward dropped to leave 26) to the front of the two-phase candidate pool, so it gets the same relaxation, SLSQP and LP refinement as the random starts.

Adds a greedy insertion constructor (grid-sampled best-fit placement of 26 circles, then a seeded smallest-circle remove-and-reinsert pass) and feeds its centers into the two-phase pool before LP and SLSQP refinement.

issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff reads no files, uses no network, pastes no coordinates and uses no labels. The new code is a crossover search (left half of one parent, right half of another, plus noise, then relaxation) over random starting layouts. The existing _relax/_score code and the final radii and validity handling are unchanged.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The crossover keeps exactly 26 circles: extras are dropped at random and missing ones are filled with random points. Centres are clipped to [0,1]. A child that fails scoring is skipped, and the loop still stops on the clock. If fewer than 2 seeds are found, the loop does not run and the code falls back to the old path.

The z value is not a real noise estimate. There is only one run per arm, so variance can't be measured. The reported z of about 11755 matches a difference of 0.0166 divided by the assumed noise floor of sqrt(2)·1e-6. Recomputed from the rounded values (-2.6131 vs -2.5965), z is about 11738. The gain of 0.0166 is real in size, but seed-to-seed variance in this stochastic search is probably far above 1e-6. One or two replicate runs are recommended before treating the gain as reliable.
Both search loops stop on the wall clock (60 s and 130 s), so how many crossover steps run depends on machine load, and results are not repeatable even with a fixed seed.

Timing margin: the search phase now runs up to 130 s instead of 80 s, adding 50 s before the unchanged refinement of the top 5. This run finished, but check the total wall time stays well inside the ~4 minute target. A slower machine could hit the 5 minute limit and crash.
The claim matches the numbers: 2.6131 is above the incumbent's 2.5965 and below the best known 2.635, which is plausible.

description: Replaces the coarse random multi-start in _two_phase with a 12-member population: seeded random packings are relaxed and LP-scored, then left/right half-recombination children are relaxed, LP-scored, and replace the worst member when better, before the top five go to the existing SLSQP polish.

Adds a fixed-seed basin-hopping stage after _two_phase that perturbs 2 to 4 centers by Gaussian noise (scale 0.05 to 0.15), re-optimises with relax, SLSQP and LP, and accepts by Metropolis at T=0.002, with the phase-1 and phase-2 time limits trimmed so the whole run finishes within about 215 s.

Adds a penalty objective (sum of squared pair and wall violations) with an exact vectorised analytic gradient over centers and radii, minimised by L-BFGS-B, and uses it in place of SLSQP in the basin-hopping local solve; LP rescoring keeps the result valid.

Adds a penalty-continuation L-BFGS-B refinement (mu from 10 growing 10x over 6 stages, joint over centers and radii, then an exact LP radius step) applied to the final basin-hopping incumbent, kept only if its exact-LP sum beats the incumbent.

Replaces the basin-hopping loop in construct_packing with simulated annealing over the 26 centers: one random center moves per step with a Gaussian scale decaying geometrically 0.1 to 0.001, each proposal is scored by the exact LP radii sum, and Metropolis acceptance uses a temperature decaying geometrically 0.01 to 1e-5, keeping the best state seen.

Adds a concentric-ring mixed-size start (1 large center circle, rings of 6, 9 and 10 with decreasing initial radii) as one seed of the _two_phase population, relaxed and LP-scored like the random starts.

Adds a discrete reinsertion (dislocation-style) move to the basin-hopping loop: with probability 0.5 a random circle is removed and reinserted at the best grid-sampled hole (maximising clearance from other centres and walls, with a small jitter), otherwise the original Gaussian perturbation is used; the usual relax, SLSQP and LP scoring and acceptance are unchanged.

Adds a power-diagram Lloyd relaxation (40000-point grid, weights r_i^2, centroid moves, LP radii after each sweep) run from the two-phase result plus four seeded random starts, keeping the best LP-scored packing before basin hopping.

Aborted: the fixed-center max-radii LP (linprog/HiGHS over radii with wall and pair constraints) is already the scoring step in _lp_radii and _score, so the only possible change is the margin, which would move the sum by about 3e-9.
Proposed a fixed-seed multi-start (default_rng(12345), K random center sets, penalty relaxation then exact LP radii, keep best) as a data-family change to train.py.

Adds a mirror-symmetric start about x = 0.5 (12 mirrored pairs plus 2 axis points) to half of the coarse-phase candidates in _two_phase; the relax, LP and SLSQP stages then run unchanged on all 26 centers, so symmetry is only a seeding bias and is not enforced in the optimisation.

Seeds the first four population members of the coarse phase with a corner-and-edge start (four corner circles, four evenly spaced circles per edge, six random interior points) before the penalty relax and LP scoring, leaving the rest of the pipeline unchanged.
Aborted: joint SLSQP over centers and radii is already in train.py as _slsqp_refine, and the proposed hex-grid start was already tested in slot 5 with no gain.
Batch 32 perturbations of the current best center set into one (32, 26, 2) array and pick the best greedy radius sum each iteration; aborted without edits.

Adds a final soft-to-hard polish: a softplus overlap penalty with analytic gradients, with beta rising from 5 to 500 under L-BFGS-B over joint centers and radii, followed by the exact LP radius step, kept only if it beats the incumbent.

Aborted: the proposed joint SLSQP over centers and radii (pair and wall constraints, bounds, maxiter cap) is already implemented in train.py as _slsqp_refine, which is applied to every candidate in _two_phase and in the basin-hopping loop.
Aborted: replacing the pairwise radius loops with a greedy approximate score is not worth a slot.

Adds a global affine squeeze-and-expand move (scale about the square center by U[0.93, 1.07] plus a per-axis shift in U[-0.02, 0.02], applied to the best packing) as a third move type in the basin-hopping loop, which then runs _relax and _slsqp_refine as before.

Adds an LP-dual sensitivity move that steps each center along dual-weighted pair-contact gradients and keeps the step only if the LP sum improves, sampled with probability 0.3 inside the basin-hopping loop under a fixed seed.

Adapts the basin-hopping Gaussian perturbation scale with a one-fifth success rule over a rolling 20-iteration window (x1.1 above 0.2 success, x0.9 below, clamped to [0.005, 0.2], starting at 0.1), keeping the fixed seed.

Adds a FIFO tabu list of the last 10 perturbed circle indices so each basin-hopping move (single-circle reinsertion or 2-4 circle jitter) samples only from circles not recently moved, with the seed and acceptance rule unchanged.

Replaces the single-chain basin-hopping loop in construct_packing with 4 replica chains on a geometric temperature ladder (0.0005 to 0.005), each doing 20 perturb/relax/SLSQP/LP steps per block, followed by Metropolis swaps between adjacent temperatures and a global best kept across all replicas, under a fixed seed and the 215 s guard.
Rattler relocation: identify loosely constrained circles from the LP contact graph and move one to the largest free hole, keeping the move only if the sum improves.

Adds a large-small center swap move to the basin-hopping loop: with probability 0.2 it swaps the centers of a random circle from the largest-radius third and one from the smallest-radius third, relaxes for 150 steps, refines with SLSQP for 80 iterations, and accepts only if the score strictly improves.

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and the RNG is seeded (31337).
The new _sym_search loop stops after 20 s of wall time, so how many candidates it tries depends on machine speed. Even with the fixed seed, results may differ slightly between runs.

_sym_search adds at least 20 s, plus polishing 3 candidates with _relax(600 iterations) and SLSQP, before the existing refinement. T0 is set before it, so any later time-budgeted loops should account for this. Still, the 4-minute margin should be checked, because a timeout would be a crash.

_relax is called with 7 positional arguments in one place and 5 in another. Its signature is not in the diff, so I can't confirm the extra arguments (0.5, c0) mean what is intended. The run did not crash, so the call is at least valid.

The candidate scores -2.636 against the incumbent's -2.6360. That is no improvement, so z = 0 (1 run each, no variance estimate) and reject is the right call. The diff makes no claims that conflict with the numbers.

description: Adds a 180-degree rotationally symmetric search (13 free centres mirrored to (1-x, 1-y), scored by LP on all 26 circles, top 3 kept, then released and polished with _relax and _slsqp_refine), and starts basin hopping from whichever of this and _two_phase scores higher.

Adds a radius-spread bonus (minus 0.05 times the sum of squared radius deviations from their mean) to the _slsqp_refine objective, annealed through three SLSQP stages (lam 0.05, 0.02, 0) so the final stage optimises the pure sum of radii.

Adds a deterministic coordinate-wise sweep after _two_phase that tries 24 fixed displacements and the 49-point hole grid for each circle, keeping a move only when the LP-scored sum rises, repeated until no circle moves or a deadline is reached.

Seeds the coarse phase of _two_phase with 24 deterministic-seeded Riesz-energy minimised configurations (exponent annealed 2, 6, 12, 24, 48 with L-BFGS-B and wall barriers) instead of uniform random starts, then passes them through the unchanged relax, score and refine pipeline.
Adds a final active-set Gauss-Newton (KKT) polish that solves the near-active pair and wall equalities for centers and radii, accepting each step only if the LP-scored valid sum improves.

Adds a fixed-seed torus (minimum-image, wall-free) repulsion relaxation, mapped affinely into [0.05, 0.95], as the start for every other coarse-phase candidate in _two_phase before the existing wall-aware relaxation and LP scoring.

Shrinking-box continuation: _relax gains an m0 argument that clips centers to an inner box [m, 1-m] with m annealed from m0 to 0, and the first coarse-phase relaxation in _two_phase uses m0=0.12, so configurations spread early and fill corners as the margin relaxes before the unchanged wall forces, SLSQP and LP scoring finish.

Adds a fixed-seed DE/rand/1/bin search (NP=30, F=0.6, CR=0.9) over the 52-dimensional centre vector, seeded from the two-phase best and scored by the exact LP sum, followed by SLSQP refinement and an accept-if-better check, capped so the total run stays under about 205 s.
Aborted without an edit: the two-tier fixed-radius start (6 large near 0.17, 20 small near 0.09, farthest-point centers) is another seeded-start variant of the kind already tried and rejected.

Adds a rigid cluster move to the basin-hopping loop: with probability 0.5 a perturbation step partitions the centers into 3 to 5 k-means clusters (fixed seed) and rotates each cluster by up to 10 degrees and translates it by up to 0.03 about its centroid, then reuses the existing relax, SLSQP, LP scoring and Metropolis acceptance.

Replaces the constant coarse-phase initial radii with log-uniform draws on [0.02, 0.12], and gives every other population member a size prior (3 to 5 circles at 0.12 to 0.15, the rest at 0.06), all from the existing fixed seed. The current coarse loop starts at 0.01, not 0.005 as the spec says, so this edit replaces that line.
Aborted: no edit proposed for the Voronoi-cluster crossover.

Replaces the hard overlap max in _relax with an annealed (beta 5 to 200) log-sum-exp soft penalty over pair gaps, and uses a soft minimum over all pair and wall gaps for the radius update; LP and SLSQP scoring are unchanged.
Hooke-Jeeves pattern search over the 52 center coordinates, scored by the exact LP sum of radii, as a final polish of the incumbent.

Adds a Lubachevsky-Stillinger style event-free growth stage (26 random-velocity centres with growing radii, wall reflection, elastic pair bounces with radius capping) whose output is relaxed, SLSQP-refined and scored as an extra member of the coarse-phase population.
Abort: the batch Bayesian-surrogate idea over layout parameters is not worth a slot, because it would not fit the time budget and the parameters it tunes have already been tested.

Aborted the Luby-sequence restart schedule for basin hopping: it would only reorder moves the loop already makes, and the same basin-hopping variants (replicas, adaptive sigma, tabu, annealing) all returned +0.0000 or worse against the -2.6360 incumbent.

Replaces the single basin-hopping chain with three interleaved chains (seeds 7, 11, 19) that share the _two_phase result as their start, and every 40 rounds copies the best chain's state into the worst chain; the time limit is shared across the chains.
Adds a per-circle weight w_i ~ U[0.6, 1.4] (drawn from the fixed-seed rng in the coarse phase) that scales each circle's radius-growth step in _relax, leaving scoring unchanged.

Abort: the row-template generator with SLSQP refinement is a near-duplicate of structured starts already rejected (corner-star seeding +0.0228, ring start +0.0066, hex-lattice start, Riesz seeding +0.0209), and the basin is saturated at -2.6360.

Seeds the coarse phase of _two_phase with fixed-seed Poisson-disk samples in [0.05, 0.95]^2 (minimum spacing drawn from U[0.12, 0.22] per seed, uniform fill if fewer than 26 points are accepted), leaving the population selection, recombination and refinement unchanged.

Aborted: seeding the coarse phase with boundary-count starts (k in 14 to 20 wall circles) is a near-duplicate of the rejected corner-and-edge seeding (slot 16, -2.6131) and ring start (slot 12, -2.6248), and the search has plateaued at -2.6360.

Adds successive-halving screening to the basin-hopping loop: each move generates 4 fixed-seed candidates, scores them after a 60-step relax with the LP, keeps the best one for a 200-step relax, and only that survivor gets the SLSQP refine and final score.

Runs the coarse-plus-crossover phase of _two_phase under three fixed seeds (2024, 31, 977), each in a one-third time window, keeps the top five per seed (15 total) for the shared relax/SLSQP/LP refinement under the same 140 s guard, and lets the existing basin hopping start from the best refined packing.

issues: No integrity problems. The diff adds a dual_annealing search over the 52 centre coordinates, scored by the existing _score LP. It reads no files, pastes no coordinates and uses no labels.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Once the deadline passes, obj returns 0.0 and the callback stops the run. The deadline is min(T0+205s, now+120s), so the job should stay within the 5-minute limit. _relax, _slsqp_refine and _make_valid still run after the deadline, but they should be short.

Minor: when the annealed centres win straight from _score (the rv_d branch), those radii skip _make_valid. This is presumably safe because the later incumbent pipeline still runs and the run did not crash.

The candidate gives -2.636 on a single run, the same as the incumbent mean of -2.6360 over a single run. The difference is about zero (to the reported precision), so the new stage gained nothing within its time budget. The z of -0.000 and the provisional reject are consistent. With n=1 on each side the variance cannot really be estimated, so z is only meaningful as 'no difference'.
A reported 2.636 is slightly above the best-known 2.635. This is presumably rounding (about 2.6359) and is the same for the incumbent, so it does not count as a mismatched claim.

description: Adds a time-boxed scipy dual_annealing stage (fixed seed 4242, 52-D centers in [0.05, 0.95]^2, objective -LP sum, callback stops at the deadline) after _two_phase, polishing its best center set with _relax and _slsqp_refine and keeping it only if it beats the current packing.

Adds a staged power-mean surrogate (maximise sum of r^p with p = 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, fixed-seed-free deterministic, 60 SLSQP iterations per stage) used only for the final refinement in _two_phase, leaving basin hopping and the population stage on the original linear _slsqp_refine.

Adds a prescribed-radius-profile population seed to _two_phase: a decreasing log-uniform target radius set is matched by Hungarian assignment (linear_sum_assignment, cost = target radius minus wall distance) to a jittered-grid site pool, then relaxed, SLSQP-refined and LP-scored before the random coarse members are drawn.

Replaces the uniform-random first population member in _two_phase's coarse phase with a deterministic farthest-point subset of 2000 base-2/base-3 Halton points, and seeds the remaining members as Gaussian (sd 0.01) perturbations of that set.

Aborted without an edit: novelty-based archive selection for the coarse population is a near-duplicate of population-rule changes already tested (slots 7, 33, 38, 43, 44), none of which beat the incumbent -2.6360.

Adds a square-grid start with one defect to the coarse phase of _two_phase: every fifth coarse-phase attempt uses a 5x5 grid at (i+0.5)/5 plus one fixed-seed random center in [0.2,0.8]^2, jittered by N(0, 0.01) and clipped to [0.05,0.95], then relaxed and scored with the same parameters as the random starts.

Adds a Delaunay edge-flip move to the basin-hopping loop: with probability 0.3 it picks a random interior Delaunay edge whose opposite vertices are not in contact and moves one endpoint to the midpoint of the opposite pair, then runs the existing relax and SLSQP refine and score-based acceptance; otherwise the existing reinsertion and Gaussian moves run.

Replaces the random basin-hopping perturbations in the second construct_packing loop with a fixed-seed (mu=4, lambda=12) evolution strategy over the 52-dimensional center vector, using a rank-mu covariance update, one-fifth-style sigma adaptation, and restarts from the incumbent.

issues: No integrity problems: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, no use of evaluation labels. The diff only adds restarts from saved good solutions (_ELITE) to the simulated-annealing loop.
The candidate (-2.636) equals the incumbent mean (-2.6360). With one run each this shows no improvement, so rejecting is consistent with the numbers.

_ELITE stores p[1] from the pool. I could not check from the diff that p[1] holds the centers. If it does not, _score should return None and the restart will not happen; neither case makes the result invalid.
The stall counter increases on every evaluation that produces a valid packing, not only on failed ones, so 60 means 60 evaluations without a new best. This is loose but not a bug.
The loop stops on a wall-clock limit (215 s), so identical runs can differ slightly. This was already true of the incumbent.
A z-score cannot strictly be computed from one run per arm (no variance estimate), but the difference is 0, so z = 0.

description: Adds a stagnation restart: after 60 consecutive basin-hopping iterations without a new global best, the current state resets to a random top-5 coarse-population member (stored in a module-level list), while the global best is never reset.

Abort: the agglomerative dimer start is another population-seeding change to the coarse phase, and this family has consistently regressed (slots 16, 27, 38, 43, 44, 45 all worsened the official value by +0.008 to +0.023 against the -2.6360 incumbent).

Aborted the delete-one-from-27 construction: it would be another population-seeding change in the family that has already been rejected repeatedly, and the time budget leaves no room for a second 26-circle search.

Aborted: multi-restart with fixed wall-count quotas (q from {12,...,20}, pinned boundary circles with a quadratic pull) is a near-duplicate of the boundary-count start idea already aborted in slot 39, and the basin is saturated, so no edit is proposed.
Log-barrier interior-path polish of the joint centres-and-radii vector, finished with the exact LP score (not run).

Replaces the Metropolis acceptance in the construct_packing basin-hopping loop with late-acceptance hill climbing: a 50-slot circular history buffer (initialised to the starting score) lets a candidate in when it beats the history entry for the current iteration or the current score, removing the temperature T.

Adds a radius-cap curriculum to the joint SLSQP: _slsqp_refine takes an rmax bound, and the final polish in _two_phase runs it at caps 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.50, warm-starting each stage and keeping the best LP-scored valid packing.

Speeds up the exact LP scoring in _lp_radii with a neighbour-list pair subset (cutoff 2.6 times the max wall bound) plus an iterative add-violated-pairs loop, so the time-boxed basin-hopping stage runs more iterations while the result stays exact; the 215-second guard is unchanged.
Abort: the fine-grid discrete annealing over occupancy is a near-duplicate of the grid-hole relocation move already in construct_packing, and the time budget is already spent.
Adds an equal-radius feasibility bisection (penalty relaxation, 12 steps) to produce a second population seed for the coarse phase of _two_phase.

Makes half of the coarse-phase random starts edge-biased by drawing coordinates from Beta(0.6, 0.6) mapped to [0.05, 0.95], alternating with the existing uniform [0.1, 0.9] starts, with the relax, score, and crossover unchanged.
Augmented Lagrangian refinement of the joint centers-and-radii vector, started from the best basin-hopping packing.
Abort the rattler-escape move: it duplicates the grid-hole reinsertion already in construct_packing's basin-hopping loop, and similar reinsertion and dislocation moves (slots 13, 46) gave no gain.
Abort: wall-contact enumeration would be another population-seeding change to a basin the notes already mark as saturated, and the spec is not a linear program as written.

Adds a 20-second fixed-seed diagonal-reflection search after _two_phase: 12 free centres and their (y, x) mirrors plus 2 diagonal points, relaxed and refined by SLSQP with symmetry released, keeping the result only if its LP-scored sum beats the current packing.

Aborted the Apollonian tangency-chain constructor: it is a greedy best-fit placement start for the coarse population, the same family as the slot 6 greedy insertion and the other population-seeding changes that all came back at +0.0000 or worse.

Langevin sampler over the 52-dimensional center vector after _two_phase, with finite-difference gradients of the LP score on 6 random circles and a Metropolis rule under a geometrically cooled temperature.

Aborted: the cosine-deformed triangular-lattice start is another population-seeding change to _two_phase, the same kind as the mirror, corner-star, Riesz, torus and ring seedings that all came back worse (+0.006 to +0.023).

Adds a sequential-LP trust-region refiner (_slp_refine, HiGHS linprog on linearised pair and wall constraints, steps accepted only when the exact LP score improves) and applies it after SLSQP in the basin-hopping loop.

Abort the cross-entropy-method stage: it is a population search over the same 52-D centre space as the DE search (slot 31) and dual_annealing (slot 41), which both left the incumbent unchanged at -2.6360.

Adds a large-neighbourhood destroy-and-repair move to the construct_packing basin-hopping loop: with probability 0.25 it removes the 5 to 7 circles nearest a fixed-seed random window centre, reinserts them one at a time at the largest-hole points on a 41x41 grid with jitter 0.004, then relaxes (150 steps) and SLSQP-refines (60 iterations) before the same Metropolis acceptance.

Adds a fixed-seed random 6-dimensional subspace search after _two_phase: for each of 30 fresh orthonormal subspaces of the 52-D center vector, Nelder-Mead optimises the 6 coefficients (each evaluation relaxes the centers toward the incumbent and scores with the exact LP), keeping any improvement, time-boxed to 170 s before the full-dimensional basin hopping resumes.

Aborted: a Hilbert-curve population seed would be another seeding change to the coarse phase of _two_phase, the same family as the rejected Poisson-disk, square-grid, Riesz, mirror and corner-star seeds (all +0.006 to +0.023 versus the -2.6360 incumbent).

Abort: the Hungarian radius-class assignment is another population-seeding change to the coarse phase of _two_phase, and the notes show that family of seeds (mirror, corner star, Riesz, prescribed profile, Poisson-disk, Hilbert, boundary counts) has been rejected repeatedly with no gain.

Beam search over greedy grid-insertion sequences (40x40 candidates, beam width 6, LP scoring at depth 26) aborted as a near-duplicate of slot 6's greedy insertion constructor and the grid-hole reinsertion already in construct_packing.

Adds a two-stage population seed to _two_phase: a 25-circle random multistart (25 s budget, fixed seed) whose best packing gets a 26th circle at the best grid hole on an 80x80 grid, then a template-guided _relax, _slsqp_refine and _score, inserted into the 12-member coarse population before the crossover stage.

Aborted: Nesterov-accelerated overlap-energy relaxation would be another variant of the _relax step that is already the core of the search, and similar relaxation and penalty variants (slots 9, 10, 29, 30, 34) all gave +0.0000 or worse.
Zeroth-order evolution-strategies ascent over the 52 center coordinates, scored by the exact LP sum of radii, as a final local refinement after the basin-hopping loop.

Aborted: a Delaunay-reduced constraint set for the SLSQP would only speed each basin-hopping step, and the basin-hopping loop is already saturated (many variants that changed moves or added iterations gave +0.0000).

Aborted: a radius-disparity penalty duplicates slot 25 (radius-spread bonus, +0.0000), and the final exact LP radius step already enforces r >= 0, so the penalty would only shift the SLSQP optimum before the LP rescoring.

Aborted the polar-coordinate reparametrisation stage: a change of variables (rho, theta) about (0.5, 0.5) is a local diffeomorphism, so the joint SLSQP would reach the same local optimum that the existing Cartesian _slsqp_refine already finds, and the stage would add wall time to a loop that already runs to 215 s.

Hierarchical n±1 transfer: run short fixed-seed searches for 25- and 27-circle packings, derive 26-circle starts by deleting the smallest-radius circle from the 27 packing and inserting a grid-hole circle into the 25 packing, and add both to the coarse-phase population.

issues: No measurement circumvention: no file or network access, no hardcoded coordinates; _mc_candidate builds its packing by seeded Monte Carlo compression starting from the incumbent's own _two_phase output.
The MC result replaces the incumbent only if its radii sum is strictly larger, and it is scored and refined by the existing _score/_slsqp_refine, so validity is unchanged.
The box-resize acceptance rule is a rough compression trick rather than a proper pressure ensemble (P grows by 1.01 per sweep). That makes it less effective, not invalid.
T0 is set before _mc_candidate, so its up to 30 s comes out of the later optimisation's time budget; it still finishes within the 5-minute limit.
Candidate -2.636 equals the incumbent's -2.636 exactly, so there is no improvement; with n=1 each there is no variance estimate and z is 0 because the difference is 0. Reject is appropriate.

description: Adds a fixed-seed hard-disk Monte Carlo compression stage (variable box side L, pressure P rising 1% per sweep, 0.02 single-circle moves and box-scale moves of 0.999 to 1.001) that starts from the two-phase result, maps back to the unit square, and runs _score and _slsqp_refine; its output replaces the starting packing for basin hopping only if its sum of radii is higher.

Aborted: a proximal bundle method over the LP value function would be a local nonsmooth optimizer on the same 52-D center space that slot 57 (sequential-LP trust-region refiner, +0.0000) and _slsqp_refine already cover.

Adds an anisotropic container continuation stage after _two_phase: SLSQP over centres and radii in widths a in {0.95, 0.975, 1.025, 1.05}, mapping x to x/a, rescoring with the exact unit-square LP, and keeping the best candidate as the start for basin hopping.
Abort the multilevel coarsening idea: it is another population-seeding change to the coarse phase of _two_phase, a family that has repeatedly returned zero or negative gain.

Aborted the elite-fraction time-allocation controller: the basin-hopping loop has only two move types in train.py (grid-hole reinsertion and local Gaussian kick), and the proposed "dislocation" move is the same grid-hole reinsertion, so the controller would only be a bandit over two moves in a basin that 30+ move and search variants have left at +0.0000.

Adds path relinking inside _two_phase: for each ordered pair of the five elite packings, match circles by linear_sum_assignment, interpolate the matched centres in 10 steps, relax each interior point with a short _relax, score it with the exact LP, and feed the best interior point into the existing SLSQP refinement pool.
Adam on an annealed softplus overlap energy with fixed radii, scored by the exact LP every 100 steps and polished by SLSQP (not run).

Adds a radius-space inflation kick to the basin-hopping loop: with probability 0.2 the current best radii are scaled by U[1.02, 1.08] and a 150-step _relax moves only the centers (lr_c 0.01, radius learning rate 0), and the existing relax, SLSQP and LP-score acceptance then run, while the grid-reinsertion and Gaussian-perturbation moves split the remaining probability.

Aborted: iterated greedy disc destruction with grid reinsertion and exact LP acceptance is a near-duplicate of slot 58 (large-neighbourhood destroy-and-repair, +0.0000) and of the existing grid-hole reinsertion and dislocation moves already in construct_packing.

Aborted the two-half divide-and-conquer start: it is another population-seeding change to the coarse phase of _two_phase, a family that has been tried about 15 times with every variant rejected (+0.008 to +0.03).

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only changes the simulated-annealing acceptance rule. It adds no file or network access, no hard-coded coordinates and no use of labels.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. h(s) = 1 - exp(-40(s - s_ref)) rises with s, so a better move is still always accepted and a worse one is accepted with probability below 1. Overflow would need s to be about 17.7 below s_ref, which cannot happen with sums near 2.6. The change only reshapes how worse moves are accepted near best_s, so the meaning of T changes.

Candidate (-2.636) and incumbent (-2.6360) are the same, so the difference is 0 and z = 0. With n = 1 on each side the spread cannot be estimated, so z is only defined as 0 because the difference is exactly 0. The provisional reject matches the numbers: no improvement was shown.
2.636 is the best-known value of about 2.6358 after rounding, so it is not a suspicious improvement over the 2.635 quoted on the card.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The Metropolis rule is replaced by a threshold rule that compares against the best score so far (record-to-record travel), with a margin D that shrinks to 0 by the 215 s deadline and a jump back to the best packing after 40 bad steps in a row. The variable T is now unused, which is harmless. span is guarded against zero. best_* is still updated only on a strict improvement. The job still runs about 215 s plus setup, which should fit under the 4-minute margin if the incumbent did.
The loop still reads the clock, so the run is not exactly repeatable even with the seed. This is the same as the incumbent and does not affect validity.

The numbers match the stated decision. Candidate -2.636 against incumbent -2.6360, one run each, gives a difference of 0, so z = 0 and reject is consistent. With n=1 on each side the variance cannot be estimated, so z rests only on the zero difference. The sum of about 2.636 is in line with the best known value (about 2.6359 before rounding), so it is not suspicious.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. Centres are clipped back into [0,1], and if no pair of circles is touching it falls back to choosing from all pairs. Adding the new branch shifts the odds of the existing moves: the old 50/50 split now applies only to the remaining 85% of iterations. This is a design choice, not an error.
Minor: np.triu_indices and all pairwise distances are recomputed on every bond move. That costs a little time inside the fixed 215 s loop but is harmless with 26 circles.
The loop stops on the clock, so results can vary by about 1e-6 between runs even with a seed. With only 1 run each, the result is not well resolved.

The numbers match. Both candidate and incumbent score -2.636, so the difference is 0 and z = 0. The variance can't be estimated from one run each, but a zero difference gives z = 0 in any case. 2.636 is consistent with the best known 2.635 (about 2.6358 before rounding), so it is not suspicious.
